newsitem.title: UK: Prudential launches bid for Scotam.
newsitem.headline: Prudential launches bid for Scotam.

text.p: Prudential Corp. Plc launched a 1.9 billion pound ($3.05 billion) bid for Scottish Amicable Wednesday, setting off a long-expected auction for the mutually owned life insurance group.

ScotAm, already the target of an offer worth more than 1.4 billion pounds ($2.2 billion) from Abbey National, said it would delay sending details of its own stock flotation plans, due to be published later this week, for at least two weeks to consider the Prudential bid and would seek further offers from other interested parties.
The Prudential offer includes a bonus payment of 800 million pounds ($1.3 billion), half of which will be in cash or Prudential shares.

The company said it would also pay 1.1 billion pounds ($1.8 billion) into ScotAm's life fund, add 150 million pounds ($241 million) to policies as soon as practicable and pay an additional 250 million pounds ($401 million) in terminal bonuses on insurance policies.
In response, Abbey National said its proposed 400 million pound ($641 million) goodwill payout to policyholders in cash or shares was a miminum level.

"Once we have access to full financial information we are sure that our final offer will be extremely attractive to Scottish Amicable's policyholders, management and staff," said Abbey Deputy Chief Executive Charles Toner.
ScotAm had been heavily criticised in recent days for pressing ahead with its own plans to shed its mutual status and eventually float the group on the stock market, in the face of the Abbey bid.

But Sandy Stewart, chairman of ScotAm said Wednesday that "From the outset, the Board has acted solely in the best interests of policyholders and we will continue to work to deliver the best result for them."
Prudential said its proposals offered substantially better value to Scottish Amicable policyholders than either the Abbey bid or ScotAm's flotation plan.

"As investors, all Scottish Amicable policyholders will benefit from Prudential's financial strength and the investment flexibility this brings," Prudential Chief Executive Sir Peter Davis said in a statement.
He said Prudential would keep and develop the ScotAm brand and retain its significant presence in Scotland.

"The essential difference between our bid and plans from Abbey and ScotAM is that we're offering to put 1.1 billion pounds into the life fund to give it the opportunity to do more equity investment," said Davis.

"We also propose to write new business in the Prudential life fund. We'd use the capital within Prudential's life fund to write the new business and as the Scottish Amicable fund, which is closed to new business, started to run off and the policies matured we'd return that capital to the owners of the business -- the policyholders -- with profits."

Other potential bidders include the Halifax building society and banking group National Westminster, as well as Belgian-Dutch financial services company Fortis, Dutch firms ING Groep and Aegon, and Australian Mutual Provident.
